findings.title: Native decoy search cannot cancel an address comparison already in progress
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The demonstrated failure requires a very large caller-selected native address scope. No secret compromise or ordinary default-scope failure was demonstrated.
affectedBuilds: native library decoy address search with two missing words and a large scan_gap
findings.prerequisites: A valid 24-word container with two missing words, an address reference with no fixed derivation path, and a large valid scan_gap. No MHFE password or Argon2 work is required.
findings.reproduction: Run target/aud016-core-public-probe through cancel_watchdog.py. The public 32-byte zero entropy phrase has words 23 and 24 replaced by ?. ContainerSearch::new enumerates 16,384 candidates. search_decoy compares against the valid Bitcoin example address 1BoatSLRHtKNngkdXEeobR76b53LETtpyT with scan_gap=2^31 and no explicit path. The first progress callback returns MhfeError::Cancelled. The Linux watchdog uses one allowed CPU and kills the process if the call has not returned two seconds after that callback.
findings.expected: The documented progress callback error stops the search, including work currently evaluating its candidates, and returns Cancelled without scanning an enormous requested address range to completion.
findings.observed: The cancellation callback is reached, but search_decoy does not return within two seconds. The retained log prints PREPARED 16384 candidates and FAIL: search has not returned two seconds after its callback returned Cancelled. Exit 1; bounded probe total 13.54 seconds. Source shows stop is checked only before compare(index). find_address has no stop check inside the account/chain/index loops; thread::scope waits for that comparison to finish before the outer error can return.
findings.impact: The documented native cancellation mechanism cannot interrupt a long address comparison. With allowed 2^31-index scopes a caller remains blocked and CPU work continues until the comparison completes or the process is terminated. The browser host can separately terminate its worker; that behavior was not classified under this finding.
findings.recommendedFix: Pass a narrow cancellation predicate or callback into the library address-search loop and check it between derived addresses. The threaded candidate coordinator should set it on the first callback error and stop reporting repeatedly after that error; reuse the same address-search implementation across callers.
findings.requiredVerification: The bounded watchdog exits 0 after cancellation at a huge valid scope. Add a deterministic native regression that waits until a comparison starts, cancels, and confirms prompt joining. Preserve address vector outputs and normal default-scope search behavior; verify the browser and CLI integration when cancellation is threaded through the shared library.

findings.title: Required native-browser acceptance assertions still expect superseded contracts
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The Chromium/Firefox job is mandatory CI and is reused by the tagged release checks job; release publish needs checks. Current source cannot pass that unchanged acceptance gate.
findings.rootCause: Production recovery/rehearsal length semantics were updated for AUD-015-FUN001, rekey now returns its declared source walletCheck field, and error wording changed, while the native-browser verifier retains earlier expected objects, refusals and progress assumptions.
findings.reproduction: Coordinator rebuilt dist as build 0ead1c7b89fe6106 and runs node scripts/verify-browsers.mjs under its serialized resource guard. Inspect original real-browsers.log. No baseline verifier edits or whole-suite reruns were performed by this reviewer.
findings.expected: Supported native-browser acceptance must assert the current documented and declared contracts, pass when production behavior satisfies them, and still reject actual mismatches.
findings.observed: The completed unchanged verifier exits 1 after 461.11 seconds: Chromium 153.0.8010.12 and Firefox 155.0, standard and fast mode, all four pages. Each has the same 17 distinct failed assertions (68 total). Failure descriptions are printed immediately and again in each page failure list. All 17 were traced to stale expectations for length precedence, extra documented rekey walletCheck fields, callback/refusal timing, case-sensitive messages or scalar error text; no new erroneous recovered entropy or key was established.
findings.impact: The mandatory acceptance gate is red and cannot validate or publish this baseline through the documented release workflow. Current observations do not demonstrate incorrect recovered entropy, encryption, wallet keys or a production bypass.
evidence: src/rehearsal.rs:369 and :488 apply AUD-015-FUN001 length rules
web/client.js:543 and web/client.d.ts:565 declare rekey walletCheck; web/core-worker.js:228 emits it
scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:333 compares message substrings case-sensitively; :354 requires TypeError and an expected substring; :410 compares exact object key sets
.github/workflows/ci.yml:75-79 invokes this verifier; .github/workflows/release.yml:93-101 requires the reusable CI checks job
findings.recommendedFix: Update the specific stale expected results to the reviewed contracts, including explicit walletCheck values and exact precedence/refusal states. Keep semantic round/output/refusal checks, separate late LENGTH_DIFFERS progress from early refusal cases, and add assertions proving the contradicted checked length cannot reach owner confirmation. Do not relax the gate to ignore arbitrary differences.
findings.requiredVerification: After remediation, rerun the unmodified supported Chromium/Firefox standard/fast matrix once against newly identified package bytes; all original semantic, callback, failure, CSP and memory checks must pass. Retain pre-fix evidence and exact post-fix counts.

findings.title: An invalid fingerprint error repeats a seed phrase pasted into the public field
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Requires a caller or user to submit secret material to the wrong public field; no remote trigger or successful recovery operation was demonstrated.

reproduction.stdin: Published zero-12 container, newline, AUD016 public synthetic password, newline, public BIP39 phrase abandon eleven times followed by about, newline.
reproduction.prerequisites: Scripted check input uses a valid public encrypted container and mistakenly places a full mnemonic in the invalid public fingerprint field.
reproduction.limits: RLIMIT_AS 512 MiB; RLIMIT_CORE 0; timeout 8 seconds; no Argon2 operation completes.

findings.expected: A malformed public identifier is refused without echoing potentially secret raw input.
findings.observed: CLI exits 2 with zero stdout bytes. Its stderr error prints all twelve mnemonic words, wrapped over multiple lines: Invalid master key fingerprint: <full public phrase> is not eight hexadecimal digits. parse_fingerprint quotes the original input, read_public propagates the error in script mode, and the main error output persists it.
findings.impact: A real mnemonic mistakenly supplied to this field could be preserved in stderr, terminal history or captured command logs, exposing spending authority. Only public test data was used. This is distinct from the original AUD-015-SEC001 missing-word search reference summary, but shares the public-input secret-boundary theme.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe the expected fingerprint syntax without repeating raw input. Apply the existing public-field secret rejection or safe error rule consistently across library and front ends.
findings.requiredVerification: A scripted invalid fingerprint containing a public mnemonic and a synthetic password emits neither raw value. Valid fingerprints still parse. Cover the interactive refusal as well as stderr and shared browser/library errors.
findings.confidence: confirmed runtime and source data flow

findings.title: Malformed worker reply envelopes throw from the page event handler and leave the operation running
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The valid packaged worker does not emit these malformed envelopes; no spending-authority exposure was demonstrated.
findings.rootCause: WorkerJob validates message names but dereferences the reply envelope and error payload without shape/type validation or a catching settlement boundary.
findings.reproduction: Run browser/page-protocol.mjs. After a valid ready reply, deliver null, {type:"error"}, or {type:"error",error:{code:"INTERNAL_ERROR",message:3}} to the actual source WorkerJob through a synthetic Worker.
findings.expected: The unknown-protocol refusal policy settles the promise with a named protocol/worker error and terminates the job. No uncaught page-handler exception or indefinitely pending job remains.
findings.observed: All three cases throw TypeError from onmessage. The promise is still pending, job.ended is false, and the worker is not terminated. The ready message already cleared the start timer. Explicit cancellation is needed to release the slot.
findings.impact: A faulty or incompatible caller-supplied worker can leave the UI waiting indefinitely, hold the long-operation slot and retain its worker memory until manual cancellation. A correctly generated worker is unaffected. This does not establish an attacker-controlled worker boundary or secret exfiltration.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate the outer reply and known-type payloads at the WorkerJob boundary; settle malformed replies through the existing named protocol refusal. Cover malformed envelopes with bounded public-class transport tests.
findings.requiredVerification: The three malformed-reply assertions reject with a named error, produce no uncaught page-handler exception, mark the job ended, terminate its worker and allow a subsequent long operation.

findings.title: Explicit null secret arguments become empty strings before the declared TypeError validation
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The exercised real-WASM calls fail safely with library refusal codes; no incorrect phrase or unchecked wallet is returned.
findings.rootCause: Nullish-coalescing defaults treat explicitly supplied null like an omitted string before encodeSecret/requireSecret can reject its type.
findings.reproduction: Run browser/real-wasm-api.mjs against rebuilt dist. Call passwords.review({password:"",passwordRepeat:null}); wallet.walletCheck({phrase:the public BIP39 fixture,passphrase:null}); and wallet.drawPhrase({passphrase:"public",passphraseRepeat:null,walletCheck:false}).
findings.expected: BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:407-412 promises TypeError for wrongly typed arguments and checks repetition types before comparison; MhfeSecret is string | Uint8Array. Explicit null is outside that type, and only walletHasPassphrase has separately documented nullable semantics.
findings.observed: The calls reject with EMPTY_PASSWORD, WALLET_CHECK_NEEDS_PASSPHRASE and PASSPHRASES_DIFFER respectively, rather than TypeError. Source probes show the null fields are encoded and sent as empty byte arrays; the real library refuses the resulting empty/mismatched values.
findings.impact: Integrators cannot consistently distinguish wrong runtime argument types from user-facing empty/mismatched secret refusals. The affected unsupported null inputs fail safely in the real package; the finding does not imply bypass of the wallet-check requirement.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply the existing shared secret-type validation to explicitly supplied values, and default only an omitted undefined value where the API permits omission.
findings.requiredVerification: All three explicit-null cases reject with TypeError; existing omitted-value and empty-string semantics retain their documented refusal/result codes; caller bytes are preserved on exceptional paths.

findings.title: The CLI reports locked secrets after a small probe passes while its actual input buffer is unlocked
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The probe establishes an inaccurate status guarantee under a restricted quota, not an actual swap write or disclosure. Best-effort locking and large-work-area limits are already part of the documented threat model.

reproduction.prerequisites: Linux RLIMIT_MEMLOCK is 4096 bytes; the directly linked current library witness is built as documented in the harness README.
steps: Run production LockProbe and production LockedText::build with 8192-byte capacity in the restricted witness process.
Under the same limit start target/release/mhfe encrypt --pim 0 --new-password own, wait for Original seed phrase, type the public partial word abandon, read VmLck, and cancel.
reproduction.limits: Separate 512 MiB address-space caps; zero core files; 4096-byte memlock quota; no cryptographic operation accepted.

findings.expected: A status claiming secrets remain locked and outside swap reflects the actual input buffers or states the successful capability probe without guaranteeing later allocations.
findings.observed: The production small LockProbe reports passed; the CLI-sized LockedText reports is_locked=false with capacity 8192. The CLI still prints kept in locked memory, out of swap while /proc/PID/status reports VmLck 0 kB with public text in its input buffer. SIGINT exits 130 and terminal settings restore.
findings.impact: Users receive a false memory-protection assurance when a small probe fits the quota but input pages do not. Later lock failures from exhaustion also cannot be ruled out by a capability probe. No swap contents, secret persistence or disclosure were measured.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the summary describe the capability probe accurately and surface actual per-buffer locking failures. If probing representative input capacity, account for concurrent buffers and avoid claiming that future allocations are guaranteed.
findings.requiredVerification: Limited and zero memlock quota, normal quota, several simultaneous buffers and later quota exhaustion produce truthful statuses. Verify real is_locked states and cancellation cleanup.
findings.historicalDistinction: AUD-007-SEC003 concerns the lifetime of locking guards; historical coverage and lock-after-write findings have different roots. This finding concerns the summary inferring all actual locks from a tiny successful probe.
findings.confidence: confirmed public API witness plus CLI runtime

findings.title: Wide Unicode password characters receive incorrect terminal cursor positions
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The observed error affects visual editing; the probe did not show different password bytes reaching the KDF or incorrect cryptographic output.

steps: Use an 80-column xterm-compatible PTY and a public fixture container with check --fingerprint --pim 0.
At Container password, type U+754C followed by ASCII a, then delete a and cancel.
reproduction.prerequisites: A terminal that displays U+754C in two cells; passwords permit Unicode.
reproduction.limits: 512 MiB child address-space cap; no KDF; SIGINT cancellation.

findings.expected: After deleting a, the cursor follows the two-cell character at one-based column 23.
findings.observed: The editor writes ESC[22G because its shown counter adds one for every character and row/column calculations assume one cell. Terminal settings restore after exit 130.
findings.impact: Deletion, replacement and wrapping can display password edits at the wrong position, confusing the visible review of the actual accepted buffer. Combining characters may have the same root, but only the wide-character case was executed.
findings.recommendedFix: Track terminal display-cell widths and appropriate character boundaries, including wide and combining characters, when calculating deletion and wrap positions. Preserve supported Unicode password semantics.
findings.requiredVerification: Wide and combining characters, mixed ASCII, wrap boundaries and repeated deletion receive correct cursor positions in representative terminal rendering. Confirm the retained password bytes still match the user input.
findings.confidence: confirmed emitted cursor sequence; no full visual terminal emulator or Unicode matrix executed

decisions.verdict: Confirmed front-end parity difference; stronger confirmation-gap wording needs qualification
decisions.severityAssessment: Medium is an owner-policy/parity judgment; Low is defensible when limited to the supported current-spec mismatch. Nonblocking as the external report states.
decisions.supported: ConfirmationNeeded::Detected refuses nonidentity references but accepts Confirmation::BuiltInCheck. A single detected short verified reading without stated mismatch or competing short lengths passes recover_confirmed_reporting. The WASM session reaches that same library route. CLI Detected always calls ask_how_to_confirm instead of offering BuiltInCheck. The library and browser documentation explicitly describe the accepted detected-short behavior.
decisions.qualification: Current mhfe_spec README:436-444 permits the detected length of a short source to pass its verifier and requires an independent reference for a reading without a verifier. Therefore this is not a violation of that current specific verifier rule. The general intended-source guarantee and AGENTS parity rule motivate the owner policy decision. A correct-password 24-word entropy deliberately shaped as one short layout, or a random wrong-password state passing the 32-bit 21-word layout, can be treated as a detected short phrase; this is source inference under the documented false-positive model, not the reproduced external runtime case.

It frees the session immediately. It does not call seal, run the public MhfeClient worker wrapper, execute the CLI, or demonstrate the claimed 24-to-21 rekey. The r1-length-rule probe checks Python length semantics against current spec bullets; it does not exercise rekey or Argon2. These evidence limits must remain visible if cited.

The source accepts a detected short reading of a 24-word original whose state accidentally passes that short verifier. AUD-016 did not independently execute that 24-word fixture in this cross-review; the probability/wallet-change impact is a source-derived conditional inference.
